ArcGIS Server Map and Feature Service Security 2023 Update 1 Patch

Published: November 20, 2023

Summary

Esri announces the ArcGIS Server Map and Feature Service Security 2023 Update 1 Patch. This security patch includes security and non-security related fixes. Esri recommends that all customers using ArcGIS Enterprise 11.0, 10.9.1, and 10.8.1 apply this patch. Refer to the section below Issues Addressed with this Patch for the list of issues resolved by these patches.

A separate patch named ArcGIS Server Security 2023 Update 1 is also available.

For users of ArcGIS Server print services, the 10.9.1 and 10.8.1 ArcGIS Server Map and Feature Service Security 2023 Update 1 Patches address BUG-000157755 which is a failure in print services when a request references both secured and non-secured services. A resolution for BUG-000157755 is also available for version 11.1 in the  ArcGIS Server 11.1 Print Service Patch.

Important Note November 20, 2023: A corrected version of this patch is available to address “BUG-000161894 - Unable to register a DB2 enterprise geodatabase as a data store or validate an existing DB2 data store in ArcGIS Server after installing the ArcGIS Server Map and Feature Service Security 2023 Update 1 Patch for versions 10.8.1 or 10.9.1.” This defect only affected versions 10.8.1 and 10.9.1. Please download and install the new setup. It is not necessary to uninstall the initial patch, the new setup will install and replace the initial patch. In the Patch Notification Tool, the new setup is listed with a B suffix on the name.

Important Note August 29, 2023: A corrected setup is available for the Windows version of ArcGIS Server 10.9.1 Map and Feature Service Security 2023 Update 1 Patch to resolve failures with the Patch Notification tool when using the Install All Patches or Install All Security Patches options, as well as a failure when installing the patch in silent mode. If you have already installed the ArcGIS Server 10.9.1 Map and Feature Service Security 2023 Update 1 Patch, there is no need to also install this new setup. The issue that was resolved is described in BUG-000160937. The Linux setup was not affected.

Issues Addressed with this patch

  • BUG-000162991 - Crash in map service export operation with clipping parameter. (10.9.1 Only)
  • BUG-000161894 - Unable to register a DB2 enterprise geodatabase as a data store or validate an existing DB2 data store in ArcGIS Server after installing the ArcGIS Server Map and Feature Service Security 2023 Update 1 Patch for versions 10.8.1 or 10.9.1.  (10.8.1 and 10.9.1 only)
  • BUG-000160937 - Installing ArcGIS Server Map and Feature Service Security 2023 Update 1 Patch from the Patch Notification options to Install All Patches or Install All Security Patches or with a silent install fails with Error 1603.
  • BUG-000158930 - North arrows missing after exporting to PDF.
  • BUG-000158920 - Map service does not include supportsQueryDomains in its root resources.
  • BUG-000158918 - Print service fails to draws map services off 11.0 or above when the web map is in one of new projections such as equal earth.
  • BUG-000158039 - There is an information disclosure issue in ArcGIS Server.
  • BUG-000157755 - Print services fail when a print request includes both secured and non-secured services from the same server. (10.9.1 and 10.8.1 only)
  • BUG-000150564 - Exporting PDFs from ArcGIS Pro 3.0 and combining them in Adobe Acrobat DC causes them to turn blank.
  • BUG-000149770 - When publishing map image layers with labels enabled in ArcGIS Pro 2.8.2 to Portal for ArcGIS (10.8.1 or 10.9.1), labels initially appear but completely disappear upon editing.
  • BUG-000124574 - Certain Living Atlas Premium content layers do not successfully display in the legend of a map printed from Web AppBuilder for ArcGIS.

Installing this patch on Windows

This patch should be installed on all ArcGIS Server installations related to the ArcGIS Server site.

The ArcGIS product listed in the table must be installed on your system before you can install a patch. Each patch setup is specific to the ArcGIS product in the list. To determine which products are installed on your system, please see the How to identify which ArcGIS products are installed section. Esri recommends that you install the patch for each product that is on your system.

The ArcGIS Server 10.9.1 Setup Program Patch is a mandatory prerequisite for installing this patch on Windows. Please download and install the ArcGIS Server 10.9.1 Setup Program Patch before attempting to install this patch.a mandatory prerequisite for installing this patch on Windows. Please download and install the ArcGIS Server 10.9.1 Setup Program Patch before attempting to install this patch.

Step 1: Download the appropriate file to a location other than your ArcGIS installation location.

ArcGIS Enterprise  
   
     ArcGIS Server 11.0 ArcGIS-110-S-MFSSEC2023U1-Patch.msp
     Checksum
     (SHA256)		 167386F304AF70E7FA9A896CEC959586B745C989F9CB8C4B86261579F7D86467
   
     ArcGIS Server 10.9.1 ArcGIS-1091-S-MFSSEC2023U1-PatchB.msp
     Checksum
     (SHA256)		 3A4D511483074BE089D609934284AFE41B89F16E90CB3EBBC40DF951F644F44F
   
     ArcGIS Server 10.8.1 ArcGIS-1081-S-MFSSEC2023U1-PatchB.msp
     Checksum
     (SHA256)		 A90DE12DC40D948D12BCE62E108858067B14297ACA96737661097735FBA3B4CE
   

Step 2: Make sure you have write access to your ArcGIS installation location.

Step 3: Double-click ArcGIS-<Version>-S-MFS-Patch.msp to start the setup process.

NOTE: If double clicking on the MSP file does not start the setup installation, you can start the setup installation manually by using the following command:

msiexec.exe /p [location of Patch]\ArcGIS-<Version>-S-MFSSEC2023U1-Patch.msp

 

Installing this patch on Linux

Complete the following install steps as the ArcGIS Install owner. The Install owner is the owner of the arcgis folder. This patch should be installed on all ArcGIS Server installations related to the ArcGIS Server site.

The ArcGIS product listed in the table must be installed on your system before you can install a patch. Each patch setup is specific to the ArcGIS product in the list. To determine which products are installed on your system, please see the How to identify which ArcGIS products are installed section. Esri recommends that you install the patch for each product that is on your system.

  1. Download the appropriate file to a location other than your ArcGIS installation location.

ArcGIS Enterprise  
   
     ArcGIS Server 11.0 ArcGIS-110-S-MFSSEC2023U1-Patch-linux.tar
     Checksum
     (SHA256)		 4B0E5CC202292DB306A66E1A25D90D919FD018A82E617C7EF3A02C4EDE38569D
   
     ArcGIS Server 10.9.1 ArcGIS-1091-S-MFSSEC2023U1-PatchB-linux.tar
     Checksum
     (SHA256)		 97A1DAED220D96E5060EF19AA9286B5EAED541251094B74043CFC90560EC07A3
   
     ArcGIS Server 10.8.1 ArcGIS-1081-S-MFSSEC2023U1-PatchB-linux.tar
     Checksum
     (SHA256)		 54FE5C19DCC7EB6137D1E7F94E905FD69590EF2001CC7A766F5A51082912C4FD
   

2. Make sure you have write access to your ArcGIS installation location, and that no one is using ArcGIS.

3. Extract the specified tar file by typing:

% tar -xvf ArcGIS-1091-S-MFSSEC2023U1-Patch-linux.tar


  4. Start the installation by typing:

% ./applypatch

This will start the dialog for the menu-driven installation procedure. Default selections are noted in parentheses ( ). To quit the installation procedure, type 'q' at any time.

Uninstalling this patch on Windows

To uninstall this patch on Windows, open the Windows Control Panel and navigate to installed programs. Make sure that "View installed updates" (upper left side of the Programs and Features dialog) is active. Select the patch name from the programs list and click Uninstall to remove the patch.

Uninstalling this patch on Linux

To remove this patch on versions 10.7 and higher, navigate to the <Product Installation Directory>/.Setup/qfe directory and run the following script as the ArcGIS Install owner:

./removepatch.sh


The removepatch.sh script allows you to uninstall previously installed patches or hot fixes. Use the -s status flag to get the list of installed patches or hot fixes ordered by date. Use the -q flag to remove patches or hot fixes in reverse chronological order by date they were installed. Type removepatch -h for usage help.

Restart your ArcGIS services.

Patch Updates

Check the Patches and Service Packs page periodically for the availability of additional patches. New information about this patch will be posted here.

How to identify which ArcGIS products are installed

To determine which ArcGIS products are installed, choose the appropriate version of the PatchFinder utility for your environment and run it from your local machine. PatchFinder will list all products, hot fixes, and patches installed on your local machine.
